saml.description: When SAML username mapping is missing or empty, Casdoor derives the username from email first and falls back to NameID if email is unavailable.
saml.note: This can make different upstream identifiers appear to merge by design if they share email or if NameID is used as fallback.

saml.description: Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively.
saml.note: Identity merges caused by configured auto-linking are by design and should not be flagged as principal-binding bugs.

saml.description: Casdoor normalizes email addresses to lowercase for uniqueness.
saml.note: Case-only differences in email should not be treated as distinct principals.

saml.description: Automatic account linking by username is case-insensitive.
saml.note: Case-only differences such as Admin vs admin may resolve to the same account by design.

saml.description: SAML providers always appear as buttons on the login page and require explicit user selection, even when only one SAML provider is configured.
saml.note: Lack of automatic redirect is by design and should not be treated as flow inconsistency.

saml.description: When an admin updates SAML provider metadata or parsed IdP settings, subsequent logins using the new trust anchor are expected.
saml.note: Do not flag acceptance under newly saved metadata as trust-anchor substitution; the admin explicitly authorized the change.

saml.description: Casdoor's SAML ACS endpoint /api/acs accepts POST only.
saml.note: GET failures at the ACS are expected and not evidence of a security issue.

saml.description: If an administrator changes provider metadata, issuer, or other trust-anchor configuration, acceptance under the new trust anchor is by design.
saml.note: Do not flag successful authentication after an admin-authorized trust change as a security violation.

saml.description: When exclusive sign-in is enabled on an application, a new sign-in removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
saml.note: Loss of an older session after a new login is expected behavior, not replay protection failure or session confusion.

saml.description: A valid bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry unless the platform documents one-time semantics.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay.

saml.description: The nbf claim is optional in JWT and lack of enforcement is spec-compliant.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf is not automatically a vulnerability.

saml.constraint: Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST use HTTP POST binding for saml_login; GET submissions are rejected by design.

For SAML tests against Casdoor as SP, the IdP/SP configuration MUST use ACS URL and SP Entity ID both set to https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Many IdP setup guides explicitly require the same value for both fields.

Casdoor SAML login is application-bound: the SAML provider must be added to the target application's Providers list before login. A configured provider that is not attached to the application will not appear on the login page and cannot be used.

SAML providers in Casdoor are user-choice flows, not auto-redirect flows. Even with a single SAML provider configured, the login page still shows a provider button and requires explicit initiation. Tests must model SP-initiated login rather than assuming automatic redirect.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, Casdoor documentation states /api/acs only accepts POST and provider metadata is parsed to fill Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider with metadata first; otherwise failures may reflect missing trust configuration rather than signature validation.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, Casdoor provider configuration derives IdP and Issuer URL from metadata via Parse. The fuzzer MUST establish a baseline login with valid metadata-derived issuer first, then mutate only the assertion Issuer/idp_entity_id. Otherwise a failure is ambiguous setup breakage.

For I2 SAML freshness tests (expired assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), include a CONTROL login using the same provider and application without the attack mutation first. Without a control, rejection may be caused by provider/application misconfiguration rather than freshness enforcement.

Casdoor supports both GET and POST SAMLResponse when acting as IdP, but when Casdoor acts as SP consuming external SAML, /api/acs accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST not infer GET acceptance from IdP-mode docs when testing SP-mode SAML login.

For I4 principal-binding tests, Casdoor documents SAML username fallback semantics: if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor first uses email as username, then falls back to NameID. Therefore multi-identity tests MUST control both email and NameID explicitly; otherwise apparent collisions may be caused by documented fallback behavior.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision tests, Casdoor may derive username from email when explicit username mapping is missing. To test whether email can override NameID, the fuzzer MUST configure or observe a provider setup where username mapping is absent, then vary email and NameID independently.

For I4 cross-protocol or account-linking tests, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. If a SAML login merges into an existing account, this may be due to configured linking behavior rather than an identity-collision bug; tests must record whether linking features are enabled on the application/provider.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens obtained after SAML-backed login, Casdoor supports RFC 8707 resource indicators. If the authorization request includes resource, the resulting access token aud becomes that resource URI instead of the client_id. The fuzzer MUST keep authorization and token-exchange resource values aligned and account for aud changing from client_id to resource URI.
Numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; it selects default behavior.

Numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration defaults to 0 hours. Documentation does not define this as literal immediate expiry in the API examples, so tests MUST verify actual behavior before using 0 as an expiry oracle.

For logout-based freshness tests, /api/sso-logout with logoutAll omitted behaves as full SSO logout by default. The fuzzer MUST set logoutAll=false explicitly when it intends to revoke only the current session; otherwise all sessions and tokens for the user may be invalidated.
Casdoor SAML SP ACS endpoint is /api/acs and accepts POST only. The fuzzer MUST send SAMLResponse via HTTP POST form submission; GET-based SAML callback tests are invalid for Casdoor as SP.

For SAML tests against Casdoor as SP, the external IdP MUST be configured with both ACS URL and SP Entity ID set to https://<your-casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Using a different Entity ID or ACS URL will cause setup failure unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, Casdoor documentation says provider metadata is parsed to fill Endpoint, IdP, and Issuer URL. The fuzzer MUST create the SAML provider with trusted metadata first, then submit forged assertions to /api/acs. A login success under attacker-signed assertions would indicate signature/trust-anchor failure; a failure before provider setup is just invalid configuration.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch, Casdoor provider configuration derives and stores IdP and Issuer URL from metadata. The fuzzer MUST vary the assertion Issuer while keeping the configured provider metadata fixed. Do NOT treat failures caused by missing or unparsable metadata as issuer-validation evidence.

For I1 saml_unsigned_assertion and saml_spurious_signature, Casdoor documentation explicitly notes that /api/acs only accepts POST and that some upstream examples configure IdPs with Sign Assertions off. The fuzzer MUST test both response-envelope-only signatures and missing assertion signatures against Casdoor SP because upstream IdPs may legitimately emit response-signed-only messages; acceptance may reflect Casdoor compatibility behavior and must be interpreted carefully.

For I2 SAML freshness tests (expired assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), the sequence MUST include a control SAML login with a valid assertion first. Without a control, rejection of the attack assertion cannot be distinguished from broken provider/application setup.

Casdoor SAML login is initiated from the login page by clicking a provider button; SAML providers do not auto-redirect even when they are the only provider. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow before posting the forged SAMLResponse so that any required request context such as RelayState/InResponseTo is established.

For I4 principal-binding tests, Casdoor's documented SAML username fallback is: configured username mapping, else email, else NameID. Therefore the fuzzer MUST control both email and NameID in crafted assertions and interpret collisions in light of this fallback order. If username mapping is absent, two different NameIDs with the same email may intentionally collapse to the same Casdoor username.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, Casdoor documentation states that when username mapping is empty it falls back first to email and then to NameID. The fuzzer MUST expect possible account linking or creation keyed by email before NameID. To test NameID isolation, omit email or ensure distinct email values.

Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. For mixed SAML/OAuth identity-collision tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish by-design admin-configured linking from unintended principal collapse.

For I5 audience-binding tests on SAML assertions, Casdoor as SP expects the SP Entity ID to be /api/acs. The fuzzer MUST craft AudienceRestriction relative to that SP entity and not to the application redirect URI or provider callback URL, otherwise failures are setup artifacts.

Numeric sentinel: application CookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning use the default cookie lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation states default is 720 hours, and without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours.

Numeric sentinel: application RefreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours unless explicitly set. The fuzzer MUST not assume refresh tokens are usable unless refresh expiry is configured on the application.

Resource indicator binding: when using the resource parameter in /login/oauth/authorize, the same resource value MUST be repeated in /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor documentation says the resource must match exactly between authorization and token requests.

For I5 token audience tests, if the authorization request includes resource=https://service.example, the resulting access token aud becomes that resource URI instead of the client_id. The fuzzer MUST inspect aud accordingly and must not treat aud!=client_id as a bug when resource was requested.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation, Casdoor documentation says omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended to narrow permissions. The fuzzer MUST request a strict subset when testing downscoping and MUST flag any exchanged token that contains broader scope or claims than the subject token.

For I2 freshness tests on OAuth tokens, use a control login with a valid token flow before testing attack conditions. Casdoor login failures can also result from disabled grant types or application misconfiguration, not just token validation.

Multi-tenant ownership semantics matter in Casdoor. Users belong to exactly one organization, while built-in/admin is the global administrator and built-in/app-built-in is the default admin application. The fuzzer MUST keep organization ownership consistent across users, applications, and SAML provider attachment to avoid false cross-tenant results.
Casdoor SAML SP consumes assertions only at POST /api/acs. Any SAML test MUST use HTTP POST binding; GET/Redirect binding to /api/acs will fail by design.

For SAML provider setup, the external IdP MUST be configured with ACS URL and SP Entity ID both equal to https://<casdoor-domain>/api/acs. Using different values breaks the flow and can be misread as issuer/audience enforcement.

For I1 SAML signature tests, application setting enableSamlAssertionSignature controls Casdoor as IdP signing behavior, not Casdoor as SP validation behavior. Do NOT use this setting as evidence that inbound assertion signatures are being validated.

Casdoor documentation states that when SAML username mapping is absent or empty, username falls back first to email and then to NameID. For I4 multi-identity tests, different upstream identities can intentionally collapse if they share email or if username mapping is omitted. Configure upstream attributes carefully and verify whether linking occurred by fallback rather than by NameID.

For I4 email-binding and account-linking tests, Casdoor supports automatic account linking by OAuth identity, email/phone if enabled, or username case-insensitively. In SAML scenarios, tests using same email across identities may merge by design unless linking is disabled or controlled.

For I4 case-confusion tests, Casdoor documentation explicitly says username-based automatic account linking is case-insensitive. 'Admin' and 'admin' may map to the same account by design; do not flag this alone as a collision bug.

For I4 verification, Casdoor identifies users in APIs as <organization>/<username>, while OIDC userinfo returns sub as the UUID user id. Do not compare sent username directly to userinfo.sub; use user record lookups or account APIs when testing principal binding.

For I5 audience-binding tests on OAuth tokens issued after SAML login, if the authorization request includes resource, Casdoor sets access_token aud to that resource URI instead of the client_id. Tests must account for this documented audience rewrite and keep resource consistent between authorize and token requests.
The OAuth authorization request and token exchange must use the same resource parameter value. A mismatch is rejected by design and must not be interpreted as a token audience vulnerability.
Numeric sentinel: application codeResendTimeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables resend delay.

Numeric sentinel: application refreshExpireInHours defaults to 0 hours unless explicitly configured. Treat 0 as effectively disabled/no refresh lifetime rather than assuming a nonzero default refresh window.

Numeric sentinel: application cookieExpireInHours uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use default'. Documentation states default is 720 hours, while sessions without Remember me are limited to 24 hours. Tests must not assume cookieExpireInHours=0 means immediate expiry.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions, include a control login with a valid assertion before sending expired or malformed assertions. Otherwise a failed login may reflect broken provider/application setup rather than assertion validation.

For I2 replay tests, application setting EnableExclusiveSignin is by-design session replacement, not assertion replay protection. A second successful login that invalidates the first session is not evidence that SAML assertion replay was prevented.

For I3 config-change tests, admin changes to provider metadata, issuer URL, or application/provider attachment are expected to take effect for subsequent logins. Do not flag acceptance under the new admin-configured trust anchor as a vulnerability.

Casdoor applications and providers are organization-scoped resources. Tests must keep owner/organization values coherent: users belong to an organization, and applications/providers must be attached so the target application can actually use the SAML provider. Wrong owner values cause setup failures that can masquerade as auth bugs.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
